persona: Defne — senior casual-mobile game designer, kids 5-7 (Peak Games / Rovio; weekly niece playtests)
headline: The core loop is real and the ladder already scales kid-to-adult, but the meta-loop is broken — progress evaporates at relaunch, the home screen shows zero state, and onboarding never makes the kid play — fix those three and 9 songs becomes a game instead of a list.

open_question_answers.recommendation: Split it: one parent page, then the kid PLAYS. Parent page (text is fine — the parent reads): device-on-piano placement diagram, mic-vs-MIDI choice, mic permission. Then no 'you're all set' page — first run auto-opens the easiest song on rung 1 (±600ms window, full glow: the kid structurally cannot fail) with Pim pointing at the glowing key and an audio cue. The tutorial IS rung 1; don't build a separate tutorial mode. The kid's verb in the first 5 seconds is 'press the glowing key and hear it land' — that's the whole FTUE. Kill the current 3 text pages; a pre-reader sees three walls of nothing.

Do NOT structure by language for v1 — no locale packs, no pick-your-language onboarding step (a pre-reader can't choose and it adds a dead screen). Language is a metadata tag (small flag/icon on the card), structure is DIFFICULTY: order the 9 songs easy→hard (Hot Cross Buns's 3 notes first, longest last) so the catalog itself is a ladder. What makes 9 songs feel complete is per-song star state on the cards — 9 songs × 4 rungs = 36 climbable challenges, and that's your store-listing math too. One real gap: you launch in Turkey with zero Turkish songs — add 2-3 (e.g. Mini Mini Bir Kuş, Ali Babanın Çiftliği) before launch. That's content, not architecture.

Cheap-but-effective = 3 static poses, not a rig: (1) Pim greeting on the home header, (2) Pim pointing in the FTUE, (3) Pim small on song cards next to the star row. Generate them on OpenArt in the CHIBI style — the reward videos already exist in chibi, so chibi is canon by default; updating the painterly icon is a later Aiko task, not a launch blocker. Do not build idle animations or new videos. Pim's job is continuity: the same character the kid meets in onboarding cheers at the result — that closes the emotional loop for the cost of three images.

The redesign IS the progression display — don't restyle the grid, give it state. Each card shows best stars (and a small rung badge once climbed); songs ordered easy→hard; Pim header on top. That single change converts 'dev-tool list' into 'game map' and is what a parent screenshots in their head before deciding not to refund. Also: move 'Add Song' and long-press delete behind a parent corner with a parental gate — right now a 5yo can delete Twinkle Twinkle with one long-press and no confirmation (HomeScreen.swift contextMenu). That's both a Kids Category requirement and a refund bomb.

Screenshot day requires four things true in-app: (1) progress persists across relaunch and is visible on home, (2) home has Pim + stars (the 'rich state' screenshot), (3) FTUE is kid-playable, (4) all 9 songs' notes are ear-verified — including the open Salta Sol-vs-Mi question — because a musical parent who hears wrong notes refunds and reviews. TR localization of parent-facing copy is mandatory for the TR launch geo. Your four screenshots then write themselves: home-with-stars, falling notes mid-play, Pim 3-star celebration, parent setup page.

Gate launch on exactly: Mei's playtest gate (kid + adult replay unprompted, miss-curve drops), persistence shipped, playable FTUE shipped, notes verified. Do NOT gate on: mascot canon, more songs beyond the TR pack, MIDI polish, locale packs. Launch TR + non-EU as planned, treat the first 2 weeks as soft launch — watch reviews and your own kid's day-3 unprompted reopen, ship a v1.1 fix, then open EU. At €1 the bar is 'no buyer's remorse in the first 5 minutes,' not D30 retention — optimize the first session, ship.

No Pim animation/rigging or icon-vs-chibi canon reconciliation before launch — 3 static poses only.
No analytics, backend, or accounts — local-only SwiftData keeps the Kids Category path clean and v1 shippable.

persona: Aiko — senior 2D art director / visual lead (kids casual mobile, ex-Toca Boca)
headline: The play loop has real warmth, but the app currently ships three different squirrels and a dev-tool home screen — one weekend of canon-locking and a Pim-led home/onboarding skin is the difference between "asset flip" and "real kids product" at €1.

open_question_answers.recommendation: Re-anchor the canon to CHIBI, not painterly — the pim-reward-assets skill says painterly is canon, but the shipped reward videos are chibi, and chibi is the correct call anyway: big head, bold 2px outline, clear silhouette reads at 60×60 where the soft painterly icon muddies. The cheap path is one OpenArt session from the already-locked Pim Character: new app icon (chibi Pim at keyboard, plain warm background, head fills ~60% of frame), a neutral waving still, a listening still, and a 'pointing at piano' still. Retire Mascot.png (it's a third, glossier squirrel). Pim then lives in exactly four places for v1: app icon, home header, onboarding guide, result screen — that's enough presence to feel like a character, not a logo.

Minimal 'designed' = three moves, no layout rework: (1) replace the system nav title with a header band — waving chibi Pim still (~80pt, gentle 2s SwiftUI bob) + rounded wordmark on a warm cream gradient background token instead of system white; (2) put the mastery stars ON each song card (empty-star row for ungamified songs — visible progression is what makes a grid feel like a game, and it's the single biggest 'complete-feeling' signal); (3) demote the dashed Add Song card to a small toolbar '+' — it's an adult feature and currently sits in the kid's grid looking like an unfinished placeholder. Keep the 8 card colors but tokenize them in a Theme.swift so the palette is enforced (max 12 colors total, Pok Pok discipline).

Visually it must become Pim-led and picture-first: page 1 = waving Pim + one line ('Play real piano with Pim!'), page 2 = a single static illustration of a tablet on a piano music stand (generate it once in OpenArt with the style suffix — this device-placement diagram is the highest-refund-prevention image in the app, because wrong placement makes mic detection 'broken'), page 3 = Pim cupping an ear for the mic ask. Kill all bullet lists; one short TR/EN line per page, icons carry meaning for pre-readers. The interactive 'play the glowing key' first-touch is Defne's FTUE design — I'll skin whatever she specs, but ship the three picture pages even if her interactive step slips.

Don't build region-pack UI or a language-picker onboarding step for v1 — that's catalog architecture for a €1 app with 9 songs. Ship everything to everyone; fix the perception visually: locale-aware SORT ORDER (tr → Turkish-friendly first, ca/es → Catalan first, else English first) plus two light section headers with icons ('Start here' / 'More songs'). 10-12 songs is the thin-feeling threshold, so add 1-3 universal pre-reader songs before launch — but stars-on-cards does more for perceived completeness than song count 9 vs 12.

Before screenshot day, five surfaces must pass the thumb test: chibi icon legible at 60×60, redesigned home with stars + Pim header, Pim onboarding pages, falling-notes gameplay with key-glow, and the 3★ Pim celebration. First three screenshots (≈70% of conversion): gameplay with Pim badge + falling notes, the home grid with stars, the celebration result screen — captioned in TR/EN, device-framed, same warm background family. No 'happy kid with iPad' stock shots. If the icon and the in-app squirrel don't match on screenshot day, fix that first; nothing else matters until the canon is one squirrel.

Launch gates from my lane only: one squirrel everywhere, home screen no longer system-white, onboarding has the placement illustration. That's roughly 4-5 days of the backlog below — then ship. Don't gate launch on more Pim videos, per-song art, or animation polish; the staged rollout / geo sequencing call is Anya's and Luca's lane.

headline: The reward layer already has soul — chroma-keyed Pim, sparkle bursts, real reduced-motion paths — but the kid and the paying parent meet a dead static grid and a text wall first; no idle, no soul, and the "thin app" refund verdict forms in the first ten seconds, so the fix is reusing the transparent-video player you already built to put a living Pim at the front door.

open_question_answers.recommendation: Kill the three bullet-point pages and make onboarding a motion demo with one live magic moment. Page 1: Pim idles and waves (reuse the chroma-key video player, new 3s clip from your existing OpenArt pipeline). Page 2: a wordless animated diagram — device slides onto a piano silhouette, a key glows, a note pops — pure SwiftUI keyframes, loops forever, zero text needed for a pre-reader. Page 3: mic permission, then a LIVE test: 'play any note' — the kid plays, the virtual key lights, Pim scale-punches in celebration. That live test IS the FTUE: it proves the magic works before the parent picks a song, and it's the single best refund insurance you can build. Per Swink, good feedback is immediate, clear, and useful — make the first feedback happen inside onboarding, not three taps later.

You already solved the hard problem — LoopingVideoView in PlayerScreen.swift does runtime chroma-key onto a CALayer with real alpha. Extract it into its own file and Pim can live anywhere for the cost of a 3-second mp4 (~500KB each, your reward clips prove it). Skip Lottie/Rive entirely: Pim is AI-generated raster art with no vector source, so Lottie means re-authoring the character in After Effects — that's a re-rig, not a port. Cheap-but-effective v1: one idle loop (breathe + blink) on the home screen header, the same idle in onboarding, static mascot.png everywhere reduced-motion is on. One new clip, one extracted view, three placements. Do NOT rig Pim in Spine until the chibi-vs-painterly canon question is settled with Aiko — animating before art lock is re-rig hell.

Motion lens only (layout is Aiko/Defne's lane): the grid needs three things to stop reading as a dev tool. One — Pim idling at the top, because a kid stops engaging when nothing moves for two seconds. Two — press feedback on every song card: squash to 0.95 then overshoot to ~1.05 on a bouncy spring, the cheapest 'this feels alive' win in kids casual; right now cards are inert NavigationLinks. Three — a staggered entrance (cards pop in 40ms apart, scale 0.9→1 with overshoot) so opening the app feels like toys arriving, not a spreadsheet loading. All three are tokens-and-tweens, no new assets except the idle clip.

Before screenshot day, the three screens that appear in the App Preview video must move: home (Pim idle + card press squash), falling-notes gameplay (already good — key glow, sparkles, pops), and the result screen (already good — star reveal, Pim clip). A 30-second preview of a static home screen kills paid conversion; motion is the product's pitch. Also fix MascotCheer before review: the code references it, the asset doesn't exist, so the reduced-motion 3-star celebration shows the same neutral squirrel — exactly the path an App Review accessibility pass will walk.

Mostly Anya/Luca's lane. My only launch gate: 100% reduced-motion coverage (it's currently ~90% — onboarding's repeating bounces are ungated) and no flashing above 3/sec anywhere (you're clean today; keep it that way). Ship when home + onboarding move; don't hold launch for more Pim poses or more juice — the gameplay layer already clears the kids-casual bar.

backlog_items.why: The current onboarding never teaches device placement or the glowing-key interaction, so the kid's first real session can fail silently — the exact 2-minute-bounce refund scenario. The live test moves the first success inside onboarding.

refund_risks: First-impression screen is a static, mascot-less grid — parent judges the €1 app as thin before the kid plays a single note.
Onboarding never teaches device placement or the glowing-key loop, so the kid's first session can fail and end in the 2-minute bounce that triggers the refund.

MascotCheer is referenced in code but missing from Assets — reduced-motion users (and pre-clip fallback) get a flat, undifferentiated 3-star result; also the path an App Review accessibility check walks.
App Preview / screenshots captured before home and onboarding move will show a dead app, depressing paid conversion and attracting exactly the disappointed buyers who refund.
do_not_do: No Lottie or Rive re-authoring of Pim — he's raster AI art with no vector source; that's a full character rebuild disguised as a format choice.
No Spine/skeletal rig for Pim in v1 — art canon (chibi vs painterly icon) isn't locked, and animating before art lock is re-rig hell, the #1 animation budget killer.
No ambient animated Pim or extra particle layers on the gameplay screen — falling notes own that attention budget, and more motion there is noise plus battery cost, not juice.

No parallax backgrounds, screen shake, or flashing celebration effects — vestibular and WCAG 2.3.1 risk for the exact 5–7 audience, and the current restrained sparkle/pop language is already at the right Pok-Pok-style volume.

persona: Khalid — senior sound designer / composer for kids casual mobile (game-sound-khalid)
headline: The app listens beautifully but answers in silence — the biggest emotional payoff (Pim + stars) plays mute, the count-in dies on the silent switch while piano notes don't, and three components are still fighting over one AVAudioSession; the €1 feeling of "finished" is an audio fix, not a feature.

open_question_answers.recommendation: Kill the three text pages and replace the core with ONE interactive sound moment: Pim points at a glowing key on the on-screen keyboard, the app plays the note (the synth already renders any pitch), the kid plays it on the real piano, the mic hears it, sparkle + Pim chirp fire. That IS the tutorial — it teaches device placement, listening, and the core loop in 30 seconds with zero reading, and it's a thin layer over the existing PitchDetector + playSparkle pipeline. No recorded speech in v1: wordless audio + demonstration is the Pok Pok/Sago path and it works identically in TR, EN, CA, ES. Keep one parent-facing setup page (mic vs MIDI, where to prop the device) — parents can read.

Pre-readers choose songs by EAR, not by locale or title — a 5-year-old recognizes the Frère Jacques melody regardless of language. So the bundling question mostly dissolves if every card can be heard: ship all 9-12 songs to everyone, sort locale-relevant ones first, and add tap-to-preview on the cards (first ~4 bars through the existing PianoSampler — songs are note data, zero new assets). Do not build a pick-your-languages onboarding step for v1; that's a text solution to a problem audio solves for free. 10-12 hearable, gamified-feeling songs is enough for €1 to not feel thin.

Pim's voice should be wordless chirps — 'squirrelese,' 5-6 one-shots: hello, encouragement, small cheer, big cheer, sympathetic 'try again.' No words means zero localization, no ElevenLabs child-voice-clone risk (their terms ban it anyway), no COPPA voice exposure, and it never goes stale. Cheapest legitimate sources: an adult voice (Onur's own) doing squeaks pitched up +4-6 semitones, or an indemnified SFX library pick — half a day either way. Then Pim 'lives' wherever the chirps fire: reward videos (currently dead silent), onboarding guide, and home-screen greeting on app open (interaction-triggered, once per launch, never looping).

From my lane, 'designed' means the home screen makes sound when touched: press a card → soft tap sound + first 4 bars of the song play on the synth piano; release or scroll → it stops. SongCardView today is title + BPM + note count — three pieces of text a 5-year-old cannot read; the preview is how a pre-reader finds Twinkle. This single change makes the grid feel alive before Aiko touches a pixel. Visual redesign itself is Aiko's call, not mine.

App Preview videos record device audio, and parents test apps with the mute switch on — so before screenshot day three things must be true: (1) the result moment sounds finished (star dings + fanfare + Pim chirp), (2) count-in and metronome are audible consistently regardless of silent switch (today they're system sounds that die on mute while the piano synth keeps playing — looks broken on camera and in hand), (3) one audio session configuration owns the app, so no 'sound went quiet after switching songs' moments mid-recording. Bounce the final mix to an old iPhone bottom speaker at 30% volume before recording the preview.

Make the silent-switch decision explicitly and ship it: this is a music-instruction app, its feedback audio is core function, so route ALL app audio through the AVAudioEngine under .playback (which already ignores the mute switch) — consistent with how every music app behaves — and offer one parent-facing sound toggle in settings as the escape hatch. Audio launch gate is small: unified session, audible count-in, sounding result screen, chirps. Do NOT gate launch on a soundtrack, voice-over, or sampled piano; the additive synth is honest and pleasant at €1.

backlog_items.title: Unify the audio session + move metronome/count-in onto the engine
backlog_items.what: Delete the rogue setCategory(.playAndRecord) calls in Metronome.prepareAudio and PitchDetector.startListening; add AudioSession.configurePlayAndRecord() so the one entry point owns both modes. Replace AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(1104) in Metronome.tick and FallingNotesScene line ~221 with a synthesized woodblock tick rendered like PianoSampler.renderSparkle and played through the engine.
backlog_items.why: Verified bug, not polish: with the mute switch on, piano notes and sparkles play (.playback ignores the switch) but the count-in and metronome are system sounds that go silent — the game appears broken at the exact first-play moment. The category race also means whoever configures last wins, producing 'sound got quiet' states. This is the #1 'it's broken, refund' vector in my lane.

backlog_items.title: Result-screen sound pass: star dings + tier fanfare
backlog_items.what: SongResultView.runSequence already pops stars one at a time with 340ms beats — fire a rising celesta ding per star (reuse renderSparkle at fixed ascending pentatonic pitches) and a ~1s synth fanfare on the 3-star burst, all through the existing engine. Hook the sympathetic low 'try again' tone on 1 star.

backlog_items.title: Pim chirp pack (wordless, COPPA-safe) wired to rewards
backlog_items.what: Produce 5-6 short wordless squirrel chirps (adult voice pitched up +4-6 semitones, or an indemnified library pack — never ElevenLabs child voices, never recordings of Deniz). Bundle as .caf, play layered over the per-tier PimResult videos (which are H.264 with no audio track — keep them mute, layer the chirp) and on the onboarding guide moment.

backlog_items.title: Home-card song previews (press to hear first 4 bars)
backlog_items.what: On card press-and-hold (or a small speaker glyph), prewarm via PianoSampler.prewarm and schedule the song's first ~4 bars from its note data at song BPM; stop on release, scroll, or navigation. One preview at a time, soft 200ms fade-out on stop.

backlog_items.why: Onboarding currently teaches nothing about the core interaction and requires reading English. A 30-second hands-on moment teaches placement + listening + the loop wordlessly, and doubles as a live mic check before the first real song — preventing 'the app doesn't hear my piano' refunds.
backlog_items.depends_on: Unify the audio session + move metronome/count-in onto the engine; Pim chirp pack (for the cheer chirp — can ship with sparkle-only fallback)

refund_risks: Mute switch on → count-in and metronome silent (system sound 1104) while piano notes still play through the .playback engine: the game looks broken on first launch, which is exactly when refunds happen.
Kid finishes the first song and the celebration — Pim video, star pops, sparkle burst — plays in total silence: the payoff moment reads 'unfinished demo' to the paying parent.
Three components (AudioSession, Metronome, PitchDetector) independently set conflicting session categories; mode/song switches can leave output quiet or ducked → 'no sound, 1 star' reviews.
Text-only English onboarding + text-only song cards: a pre-reader can't start or even pick a song without a parent reading for them — kid bounces in 2 minutes, parent refunds.
do_not_do: No recorded speech/VO in any language for v1 — wordless chirps + demonstration only; speech means 4-locale recording/maintenance and review burden a €1 app can't carry.

No background music bed or autoplay ambient — this is a piano app, the kid's piano IS the music; keep the verified interaction-triggered architecture (also keeps WCAG 1.4.2 and parent-in-restaurant tolerance solved).
No audio middleware migration (FMOD/full AudioKit) and no 25 MB Salamander SF2 bundle — the AVAudioEngine additive synth is right-sized and honest at €1; revisit sampled piano at €5.
No AI-generated music from tools where you don't own or aren't indemnified for the output (Stable Audio especially); for the tiny fanfare/tick needs here, synthesize in-code — you own every sample.

persona: Mei — senior kid-research / playtest specialist (ages 3-12, sweet spot 5-7), 2,000+ kid sessions
headline: The first two minutes belong to adults, not the kid: a pre-reader walks past three text pages and a dead mic promise into a dense English-only toolbar where nothing happens until someone finds a small "Play" button — fix that cold open and the input honesty, and the €1 holds.

open_question_answers.recommendation: Replace the 3 text pages with a 60-second playable FTUE in two parts. Part 1 (parent, ~20s): one picture-based setup screen — 'How will you play?' with two illustrated choices, touch-the-screen or USB keyboard (photo of iPad propped on a piano with the camera-adapter cable) — and DELETE the mic permission page entirely, because I verified startListening() is never called: the app requests a permission for a feature that does not exist, which is both a refund trap and an App Store review smell. Part 2 (kid, ~40s): Pim points at ONE glowing key, kid presses it, sparkle + sound; repeat with 3 keys; then auto-launch Salta rung 1 with the count-in. Zero reading required — the kid learns the core interaction by doing it, which is the only way a 5-year-old learns anything.

9 songs is enough for €1 — the thinness feeling comes from 8 of 9 songs ending in a flat text overlay with no stars and no Pim, not from catalog size. Do NOT build locale-pack infrastructure for v1: ship all songs to everyone, and remember pre-readers pick by PICTURE, not title — give every song card an icon (sheep for Mary, star for Twinkle, squirrel for Salta) and let locale merely sort the grid (familiar songs first). A pick-your-language onboarding step is an adult abstraction a 5-year-old cannot answer; skip it. Add Turkish songs later as a free update — 'new free songs' is also your best post-launch review driver.

Kids attach to a character through repetition of the SAME pose, not through animation everywhere. Cheap-but-effective v1: (1) Pim static greeter on the home screen header, one pose, (2) Pim as the FTUE guide pointing at the glowing key (same still asset), (3) the existing reward videos. That is three touchpoints in every session — enough for a 5-year-old to call it 'the squirrel game.' Reconciling chibi-vs-painterly icon canon matters for the parent's first impression on the store page (Aiko's call), but in-app, consistency of pose beats quantity of appearances.

'Designed' for this app means the home screen answers a pre-reader's two questions: 'which one is my song?' (per-song picture icons) and 'how am I doing?' (best-stars row on each card, persisted). Add the Pim greeter and move Add Song + delete out of kid reach — delete is currently a long-press context menu on every card, which a mashing 5-year-old WILL trigger, and a vanished favorite song reads as 'app broke' to the parent. That's the whole redesign; no hero illustration needed for v1.

Four in-app gates before screenshot day, in order: (1) the mic claim is resolved — removed from onboarding and never promised in store copy, because a parent with an acoustic piano who buys 'the app hears your piano' gets a 100%-justified refund; (2) every song ends in the same stars+Pim result so any screenshot you take is true of the whole app; (3) TR+EN strings exist — today there is zero localization in the codebase; (4) one cold-start kid gate passes: a 5-year-old you are not the parent of reaches their first deliberate correct-key press in under 90 seconds with zero adult words. Screenshots of the result screen and falling notes are your money shots; they must depict the median song, not the one gamified song.

Launch is your playtest at scale, so structure it like one: before the button-press, run the already-written protocol (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-08-playtest-protocol.md) with 5 age-5 kids — recruiting takes lead time, start now — and treat ≥3/5 day-3 unprompted reopens as the go signal. Then soft-launch Turkey-first as planned, with refund rate and 1-2 star reviews as your only metrics (if you pick Kids Category there is no analytics, and that's fine — reviews ARE the kid data at €1 volume). Do not wait for Pim canon, more gamified songs, or mic support; ship when the four store gates pass and iterate from reviews.

Reuses PianoKeyboardView glow + existing Pim assets.

backlog_items.title: Cold-open playtest gate: 5 age-5 kids, 120-second first-touch block
backlog_items.what: Extend the existing playtest protocol with a cold-open block: hand the device at the home screen, say nothing, measure time-to-first-deliberate-correct-key and where each kid stalls. persona: Marco — senior solo-dev game programmer (tech stack + architecture)
headline: The game core is solid and the mastery ladder is already song-generic — but the data layer is not ready for a catalog: the shipping build seeds exactly ONE song, seeding deletes user songs by title match, rung progress dies on every launch, and the en/es Localizable.strings are not even in the Xcode resources build phase, so nothing localizes today.

open_question_answers.recommendation: Yes, reuse FallingNotesScene as the tutorial — I verified it is fully song-agnostic: it takes any Song, reads the shared clock from PlayerViewModel, and gets geometry from KeyboardLayout.default. The tutorial is just a 3-note 'song' (Do-Re-Mi) run at rung-1 settings (50bpm, full glow, ±600ms) launched from onboarding; the kid plays the actual game in minute one, no new engine, no new dependency. Keep exactly ONE parent page before it: two big buttons (mic vs USB MIDI) plus an illustrated device-placement picture. Kill the three text-bullet pages in OnboardingView.swift — they teach nothing a pre-reader can use. This is 1-2 days, not a project.

Ship ALL songs in the binary — each song's notes are ~1-2KB of JSON, so the entire 15-song catalog costs less than one Pim video frame. Packs, on-demand resources, or IAP gating is over-engineering for a €1 app; bundling cost is zero. Surface by locale: section the home grid (e.g. 'Your songs' = Locale-matched language first, then 'More songs'), no pick-your-language onboarding step. BUT the Song model needs surgery first: add a stable seedID and localized-title map, and stop keying seeds on raw title — SeedData.seedIfNeeded currently DELETES any song whose title matches a retired seed, which will eat a user-created 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star'. 12-15 songs (4 EN global, 4 TR, 3-4 CA, 2-3 ES) is enough to not feel thin; 8 already exist in git history. Also add dotted notes + rests to NoteDuration (S effort) or half the Turkish repertoire won't transcribe; skip triplets.

From the tech side: do NOT add Lottie/Rive/Spine runtime for v1 — that is a dependency tax and binary cost for a €1 app. The code already has the cheap path built: SongResultView falls back to 'Mascot'/'MascotCheer' static assets, and LoopingVideoView (custom chroma-key player) exists and works. Cheap-but-effective = 2-3 static Pim poses (OpenArt) dropped into Assets for home header, onboarding guide, and empty states, plus the existing reward videos where they already play. Which poses and the canon reconciliation is Aiko's call, not mine — but the engineering answer is 'static PNGs, zero new dependencies.'

The LazyVGrid is fine — keep it. What makes HomeScreen feel like a dev tool is missing DATA, not missing design tech: there is no per-song progress to show because rungIndex lives only in memory (PlayerViewModel comment admits 'persisting best-rung across launches is backlog'). Add bestStars/bestRung as additive SwiftData fields (safe lightweight migration), render star/rung badges on SongCardView, add locale sections and a Pim header. Also move 'Add Song' and delete-via-context-menu behind a parental gate — a 5yo can currently delete every song with a long-press, and Kids Category will require the gate anyway.

Four things must be true in-app before screenshot day, all verified gaps: (1) the catalog is restored — the current build seeds only Plim Plim (SeedData.createSeedSongs returns [plimPlim()]); a parent who pays €1 and sees one song refunds in the first minute; (2) the mastery ladder runs on every song — good news: MasteryLadder/Rung/HitJudge are already fully generic, only persistence and per-song reward gating are missing; (3) TR localization actually ships — the .lproj files exist on disk but are NOT in the PBXResourcesBuildPhase, so today every string renders in English regardless of device language; migrate to a String Catalog and wire it in; (4) mic input drives the game mode — see refund risks.

The local-only, no-backend, no-SDK architecture is the correct launch architecture — do not touch it. Zero third-party SDKs means Kids Category compliance is nearly free and there is no privacy-label work; keep it that way until the Kids decision lands, and do NOT add an analytics SDK before launch. Binary is small (~3MB of videos, abcjs, one Swift package). Launch gate = the device playtest in product/backlog.md passes + one crash-free TestFlight week with the restored catalog. That is the whole bar; everything else is post-launch iteration.

Home grid gets two sections: locale-matched songs first, then the rest. Add dotted-note + rest support to NoteDuration where transcriptions need it.

refund_risks: Shipping build seeds exactly ONE song (SeedData.createSeedSongs = [plimPlim()]) — parent opens a €1 app, sees one song, refunds. The brief's '9 seeded songs' is stale.

persona: Luca — senior mobile marketing / UA / launch strategist (kids casual), game-marketing-luca
headline: The product can earn its €1, but today it's a TR-first launch with zero Turkish songs, a mic feature that will be blamed as "broken," and one gamified song — fix those three and the refund problem mostly disappears, because at €1 nobody refunds for value, they refund (and 1-star) for "it doesn't work" or "it's a prototype."

open_question_answers.recommendation: From my lens, onboarding has exactly one commercial job: prove the app works within 60 seconds of purchase, because 'mic didn't hear my piano' is your #1 refund/1-star driver. V1 = 3 beats: (1) Pim shows 'put the device on the piano' (illustration, no text wall), (2) mic permission with a pre-prompt explaining why, (3) the magic moment — 'play any key' and the app names the note it heard, live, with a troubleshooting fallback (move closer, reduce noise, or plug in MIDI). The kid-FTUE game layer is Defne's call; I only insist the parent-setup proof-of-life ships in v1. Current OnboardingView.swift is 3 text pages — that's a refund generator, not onboarding.

All songs included at €1 — no IAP, no packs-for-sale. That keeps the trust stack ('one price, no ads, no subscriptions, nothing to unlock') intact and Kids Category filing simple. Structure: add a language field to Song (Song.swift has none today — verified), default-sort by device locale with the rest below, optional language chips in onboarding. The catalog IS the wedge: Simply Piano/Yousician are English-centric subscriptions; you are 'folk songs your kid already knows, in your language, for €1.' Minimum to not feel thin: 12-15 songs with at least 3-5 in the buyer's language — which means 3 Turkish songs are mandatory before any TR push (you have zero; SeedData.swift confirms 6 EN/universal + 3 Catalan).

Mostly outside my lane (Aiko/Diego own execution), but the marketing constraint is mine: Pim is your only brand asset and must appear in screenshot frame 1 and in the first 10 seconds of app use, or the icon is writing a check the app doesn't cash — that mismatch reads as 'asset-flip' to a parent and feeds refunds. Cheap version: reuse existing reward-video stills/poses as a static Pim greeter on home and as the onboarding guide. Do not commission new animation before Aiko reconciles the chibi-vs-painterly canon.

Treat home as App Store screenshot frame #1 — that's the design brief. It must show, at a glance: Pim, stars/progress per song, and language-grouped song cards, so a parent screenshot-skimming the listing reads 'finished product with progression,' not 'dev tool' (current HomeScreen.swift is a 113-line plain grid). Visual execution is Aiko's; my acceptance test is brutal and simple: would this screen survive in a 1290×2796 store frame next to Pok Pok's?

Before screenshot day, four things must be true in-app: ≥12 songs with stars visible on home, the mic magic-moment onboarding, Pim present outside reward videos, and mastery on more than one song (one gamified song cannot honestly fill a 3-5 frame arc). Two decisions to make now, not at submission: file IN the Kids Category — you're local-only SwiftData with no analytics, so the 1.3 restrictions cost you nothing and parents browse that shelf on trust; and 'No Data Collected' on the privacy label is a marketing weapon — put 'no ads · no subscriptions · no data collected' as a dedicated trust frame. Then route keyword/metadata work to /jpm-aso.

No paid UA, full stop: €0.85 net per sale vs ~$1.41 casual iOS CPI (Liftoff 2025) is structurally underwater forever at €1 — your entire plan is organic, which is fine. Sequence: (1) quiet technical launch TR + non-EU (this is a crash/refund shakeout, NOT a retention read — TR metrics run 30-50% below global, ignore them); (2) first real marketing beat is niche-first Catalonia once EU is on: 3 Catalan kids songs in a piano app is genuinely rare — pitch Catalan parenting communities, criança-en-català blogs/Telegram groups, and Catalan family influencers with the 'Sol Solet on a real piano' story; (3) TR push only after Turkish songs ship; (4) submit an Apple Featuring Nomination on every release and a Common Sense Media submission at launch — as upside, never as the plan. Your 'good enough to launch' gate is the completeness checklist above plus a clean TestFlight device test, not metrics — at this volume cohort tables don't exist; your scoreboard is App Store Connect refund count and rating average.

persona: ASO / Store Presence lead (jpm-aso + appstore-screenshots + appstore-release)
headline: The app is accidentally almost Kids-Category-compliant (zero data collection, no network code) but has three silent submission blockers — no Turkish localization in an app whose primary market is Turkey, an iPad-only build that contradicts store-config.md's iPhone screenshot plan, and no privacy policy — all cheaper to fix than any screenshot.

open_question_answers.recommendation: Kids Category: NO for v1. It is a one-way door (leaving later requires Apple's blessing), it permanently forbids third-party analytics, and mic access inside Kids Category triggers extended review — the worst trade for a solo dev racing to launch. You lose almost nothing: paid €1 discovery is search-driven, not Kids-tab browsing (which skews free). Instead: age rating 4+, privacy nutrition label 'Data Not Collected' (true today — I verified no network/analytics code exists), and App Review notes stating pitch detection is on-device, nothing recorded or transmitted. Guideline 5.1.4 still applies because the metadata targets kids, but zero collection satisfies it for free.

Metadata per locale: TR title 'Y La Piano – Çocuk Piyanosu' / subtitle 'Gerçek piyanoda şarkı öğren'; EN title 'Y La Piano – Piano for Kids' / subtitle 'Learn songs on a real piano' (all ≤30 chars). Keywords field (100 chars): never repeat title/subtitle words — TR: klavye,müzik,nota,ders,oyun,bebek,başlangıç,kulak; EN: keyboard,music,notes,toddler,lessons,midi,beginner,ear,training. Note the TR storefront also indexes English (UK) metadata, so EN keywords work double-duty in Turkey. ES/CA later: Catalan is not an App Store locale — put Catalan song-name terms (castanyera, cançons) inside the es-ES keywords field. Listing completeness checklist beyond text: privacy policy URL (REQUIRED, missing), support URL, age-rating questionnaire, privacy labels, iPad 13" screenshots only (the app is TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY=2 — fix store-config.md, which wrongly plans iPhone 6.7" frames).

What must exist in-app before screenshot day (the frame-arc gate): (1) home screen redesign shipped — the current LazyVGrid dev-grid would be frame 2 and would kill conversion or, worse, force you to screenshot something the buyer never sees, which is the #1 refund setup; (2) Pim visible on home + reward so the icon's mascot promise is kept; (3) tr.lproj exists so TR renders are real UI, not English screenshots on the Turkish storefront; (4) star/progress display on song cards so a 'progress' frame is honest; (5) a deterministic seed mechanism (launch argument) for each frame state. Frame arc: 4 frames — falling-notes hero mid-song, 'hears your real piano' (mic/MIDI), Pim reward celebration, song library with progress. Don't pad to 8.

Don't build locale-gated packs — ship all songs to everyone and localize the song TITLES per locale instead. Three of your nine songs already ARE Turkish classics under English names: Twinkle Twinkle = 'Daha Dün Annemizin', Old MacDonald = 'Ali Baba'nın Çiftliği', Frère Jacques = 'Tembel Çocuk'. That's a half-day strings change that makes the catalog feel native in your primary market, versus zero TR-recognizable songs today. Sort order by device locale (TR-recognized first on TR devices) is the only 'bundling' v1 needs. Nine-to-twelve visible songs is plenty for €1 — thinness perception comes from the dev-tool home screen and one-of-nine gamified songs, not the count.

Soft-launch sequencing, not perfection: submit to Turkey-only first (primary market, cheapest place to absorb a bad review or a rejection), watch 7 days for refunds/crashes/review feedback, then expand EN storefronts + EU in one release. Use the existing appstore-release flow (notes per locale, char-verified, stop before Submit). Biggest rejection risk is the reviewer questioning a kids-marketed app with mic access — pre-empt it entirely in the Review Notes field with a 2-line explanation plus a demo tip ('hum or play any tone near the iPad'). Gate launch on the screenshot-prereq list above, not on gamifying all nine songs.

From the store/review lens: keep a pre-permission priming screen BEFORE the iOS mic dialog (you have one — good), but add a 10-second live mic check ('play any key — see it light up') at the end of onboarding. It doubles as setup verification (device placement on the piano) and is your cheapest defense against the 'it doesn't hear my piano' refund, which for a mic-based app is the dominant refund category. Also localize the NSMicrophoneUsageDescription via InfoPlist.strings — today it exists in English only, which looks sloppy to a TR reviewer and a TR parent.

persona: Market Reality / Discovery PM (jpm-discovery lens) — competitive scan, pricing, catalog economics
headline: The wedge is real — every credible competitor (Simply Piano, Yousician, Flowkey, Piano Maestro, Skoove) is a $60–170/yr freemium subscription and nobody serves local-language folk songs at a one-time price — but launching Turkey-first with zero Turkish songs in SeedData.swift and only 1 of 9 songs gamified is the actual refund machine, not missing polish.

open_question_answers.recommendation: Ship ALL songs to ALL buyers — never locale-gate content; hidden songs make a €1 app feel thinner, and catalog size IS the perceived value at this price. Surface by locale: device language picks section ordering on home (TR device sees 'Türkçe şarkılar' first, then 'In English', 'En català'). The killer gap: launch geo is Turkey-first and the seed data has ZERO Turkish songs — add 4 (Mini Mini Bir Kuş, Ali Babanın Çiftliği, Yağ Satarım Bal Satarım, Kırmızı Balık) before any launch. Target 12–14 songs total for €1; that's enough if (and only if) every song works in game mode. Skip the pick-your-languages onboarding step for v1 — it's a setting nobody needs when everything is included.

Positioning writes itself from the competitive scan: 'Real piano. No subscription. No ads. Songs in your language.' — that's the sentence every screenshot must prove, because subscription fatigue is the entire reason a parent picks €1-once over free-to-download Simply Piano. Before screenshot day, three things must be true in-app: every song launches the falling-notes game (screenshots will show game mode — if 8 of 9 songs don't have it, that's the oversell that triggers refunds), Turkish songs exist, and the home screen shows per-song stars so a 'progress' frame isn't fiction. Mention the song count and languages explicitly in the listing copy.

Soft-launch Turkey-only at €1, exactly as planned — but treat it as a review-collection sprint, not a revenue event. At this price the threat isn't refunds (Apple refunds on €1 are rare; 60% of parents don't even bother) — it's 1–2 star 'doesn't work / boş uygulama' reviews permanently poisoning a listing with 10 ratings. Get 10–15 honest ratings from TR friends/family + the Catalan circle in week one, fix whatever they hit, then open EU. Zero paid UA. Your only marketing asset is the true story — 'a dad built this for his daughter Deniz' — use it in the listing and one post in TR/Catalan parenting communities.

Market lens: competitors get you playing a real note inside 60 seconds — and your single biggest refund scenario is 'mic detection didn't hear my piano.' So v1 onboarding = a 90-second interactive mic check disguised as a game: Pim asks for the mic, parent places device on piano (one illustration), kid plays ANY key and the app celebrates naming the note, then 3 glowing-key hits → confetti. This simultaneously teaches the core interaction AND verifies the buyer's hardware works before they can conclude the app is broken. Include a 'didn't hear it?' fallback (move device / reduce noise / use USB MIDI). Replace the 3 text pages; pre-readers can't read them anyway.

Cheap version only: static Pim poses (export stills from the existing reward mp4s, keep one canon style) in three spots — onboarding guide, home-screen header, and the post-song result. Do NOT commission new animation or reconcile the icon/mascot canon before launch; no €1 buyer refunds over mascot style inconsistency, and the committee's Aiko track owns that later.

From the market lens the home screen has one job: look like the screenshots and not like a dev tool. Minimum 'designed': language sections, star count per song card, Pim header, and a visible 'next song to try' nudge. That's it — it's a catalog browser for 12 songs, not a metagame map.

do_not_do: Don't build IAP song packs, regional bundles, or locale-gated content — one price, everything included; gating makes a €1 app feel thinner and adds Kids-Category/parental-gate complexity.

Don't add a backend, accounts, or third-party analytics to 'measure the market' — at this scale, sales + reviews ARE the analytics, and Kids Category may forbid the SDKs anyway.
